newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW-AMF bowls for dollars in South America.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-AMF bowls for dollars in South America.

text.p: U.S.-based AMF Bowling Worldwide said its new joint venture in Argentina and Brazil is destined to grow to become the world's third largest chain of bowling centers in five years.
"This is a huge opportunity," AMF President Douglas Stanard said in a telephone interview.

The comments came late Tuesday after AMF and Brazilian leisure and recreation firm Playcenter SA announced they planned to invest $100 million over five years to develop and run 39 bowling alleys in Brazil and Argentina.

The Sao Paulo-based joint venture, called AMF Playcenter, is AMF's first major move into the emerging South American leisure and recreation market and will be the company's main effort in the region in the coming years.
"As far as this venture is concerned, our main focus for the next years will be in Brazil and Argentina," Stanard said.
Stanard said Richmond, Va., based AMF decided to move into the region as a builder and operator of bowling centers as a result of the strength of its existing relationship with Playcenter.
"We believe that Playcenter's dominant position in the South American recreation market will contribute significantly to the expansion of bowling on the continent," he said.
He said the economic changes sweeping the region also were important "insofar as there's a good climate. Certainly the economy, if it is growing, etc, is important," he added.
Stanard said AMF, the largest bowling center operator in the United States, has no immediate plans to expand in South America outside Brazil and Argentina.
Although it is not yet as popular as it is in the United States, bowling is likely to catch on in South America as it has elsewhere in the world, he said.
Despite some misconceptions it is mainly an American pastime, Egyptians invented the sport thousands of years ago and today some 100 million people around the world go bowling every year, he said.
"Only we Americans make the mistake of thinking its American," Stanard said. "The truth is there are 12,000 bowling centers around the world, more than half of them outside the United States."
